description: Continuous Distribution Experimentation Framework: Testing Hooks, Formats, CTAs, and Repurposing Angles across External Channels.

experiments.name: LinkedIn Hook Style: Contrarian Question vs Direct Data Claim
experiments.hypothesis: Opening with a bold, counterintuitive data point ('Analyzing 448k channels showed median best video is 10.82x first upload') will generate 40% higher outbound referral clicks than a general question ('How do you evaluate creator performance?').

experiments.name: X Thread Link Placement: Tweet 1 vs Final Tweet vs Auto-Plug
experiments.hypothesis: Placing the canonical research link in the final tweet of a 5-tweet analytical breakdown will preserve thread reach by 3x compared to linking in Tweet 1, resulting in higher net referral traffic.

experiments.name: YouTube Shorts CTA: Direct Extension Name vs Visual Workflow Tease
experiments.hypothesis: Ending a 30-second research short by demonstrating the live CSV export button generates higher install intent than verbally pitching the extension by name.

experiments.name: Newsletter Framing: Standalone Tactical Guide vs Editorial Synthesis
experiments.hypothesis: Formatting the weekly newsletter as a dedicated 'Data Drop' with 1 chart and 1 actionable workflow will produce a 25% higher click-to-open rate than a multi-link link digest.
